content\n###  [Course Terms and Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Two people sitting at a desk, looking at a laptop screen together.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-29693.jpg)\n**Succeed with a Masters designed around the needs of today\'s finance-driven organisations and gain a head start in a rewarding career.**\nCareers in accounting and finance are rewarding but extremely competitive. To succeed, you’ll need essential academic knowledge and the practical skills to apply it in a professional environment. This programme covers both, giving you a decisive advantage as you progress to the next step of your career. \nYou’ll build a dynamic blend of technical accounting expertise and advanced financial knowledge, focusing on essential skills such as financial reporting standards, performance evaluation, and capital management. \nThe MSc Accounting and Finance combines research-led teaching from our cutting-edge research centres. With a focus on practical quantitative skills, your learning is grounded in up-to-date industry insights and real-world data analysis. \nYou’ll enjoy a challenging, rewarding and rounded learning experience, covering fundamental topics such as corporate finance and corporate reporting while exploring emerging trends. Optional modules allow you to specialise in areas such as forensic accounting and Python programming for finance. \nOur inspirational academics are influential thinkers with a real passion for their subject. Experts in their field, they have extensive teaching, research and internationally renowned consultancy experience, all of which feeds into the course. \n> _“The comprehensive curriculum closely related to the industry has equipped me with in-depth knowledge and practical skills in the fields of accounting and finance. For example, through the corporate finance courses, I mastered some analytical methods, such as foreign exchange arbitrage, that are highly valued in the financial industry.”_\n> _[Chongfang Yuan, MSc Accounting and Finance](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/finance/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/2348/chongfang-yuan?searchDirCategoryID=10007) _\n### Why study at Leeds \n  * **Prestigious triple accreditation:** Our Business School is [triple-accredited](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations), and this course is supported by a partnership with the [CQF Institute](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcqfinstitute.org%2F&data=05%7C02%7CL.F.Emmans%40leeds.ac.uk%7C81c888cfea3f4343299708de0d74130a%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638962989359513400%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=EevKB6S6A6JU4vpw0J%2FpOSxDc31%2F6t0D%2FsdBjxZ3bDg%3D&reserved=0), the awarding body for the Certificate in Quantitative Finance (CQF).\n  * **Dedicated employability officers** : Benefit from personalised career support for financial professions.\n  * **Be supported to succeed** : Benefit from small tutorial groups and regular one-to-one meetings with academic staff to ask questions and discuss your work.\n  * **Gain up-to-the-minute insight** : Strong relationships with the accounting, finance and credit professions give you the latest practitioner, policy and regulatory developments. Guest speakers have included a UBS non-executive board member and members of the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee.\n  * **Flexible, bespoke module options** : Tailor your studies across financial knowledge and technical accounting fields in line with your interests and specialism.\n  * **Practical teaching in cutting-edge facilities** : Deepen your understanding of real-time financial analysis, data interpretation and investment decision-making through studies that develop your practical skills. Our [financial markets lab](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/departments-accounting-finance/doc/databases) provides access to tools and platforms including Bloomberg, WRDS, CSMAR, Refinitiv Eikon, and Datastream.\n  * **Advanced specialist research units** : We have strong links with leading institutions in the US, Europe, and Asia. These include the [Centre for Advanced Study in Finance (CASIF)](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-casif), the [International Banking Institute (IBI)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-ibi), the [Centre for Financial Technology (Fintech)](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-fintech), and the [Credit Management Research Centre (CMRC)](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-cmrc).\n\n\n### Accreditation\nThe MSc Accounting and Finance programme provides extensive exemptions from the examinations for the professional qualifications of the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA).\nWe are affiliated with the CFA Institute (Chartered Financial Analyst) as a member of the [CFA® University Affiliation Program.](https://www.cfainstitute.org/en/about/universities/university-affiliation#q=leeds&sort=%40titlewithfallback%20ascending&f:CountryRegion=%5BUnited%20Kingdom%5D) Eligible students can apply for CFA® scholarships that cover the cost of registration for the CFA examination.\nLeeds University Business School has triple accreditation from the three leading bodies: AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS.\nThis means you\'ll join one of the UK\'s most prestigious business schools with a global reputation for high-quality teaching and research. We’ll introduce you to a culture of new ideas and different perspectives. Our diverse, international learning community will offer you new experiences and global connections for life.\n[Find out more](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbusiness.leeds.ac.uk%2Fmasters&data=05%7C02%7CA.C.Chadfield%40leeds.ac.uk%7Ccf8621422c6945eb5dea08ddf53134f7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638936313893473135%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Y3Uy2qyKe1OxlwacoIGU8mvtpN6VTXzGVYElWvLKT6Y%3D&reserved=0)\n## Course details and modules\nYou\'ll explore the essentials of corporate finance and the relationship between accounting information and organisational performance. \nAt the same time, you\'ll build advanced skills in handling quantitative data and examine how modern finance theories are applied to solve complex finance problems. \nYou\'ll develop your critical thinking and analytical skills, gaining an understanding of important research methods in finance and their impact on current practice. \nYou\'ll gain specialist knowledge with your choice of optional modules in a range of subject areas, such as behavioural finance, international banking and finance, international investment, and information and organisation design. \nTo demonstrate the knowledge and skills you acquire during the course, you’ll design and carry out your own research dissertation in the final semester. This allows you to focus on a topic of your choice, developing your ability to tackle the most pressing challenges currently facing the industry. \nThroughout the course we’ll support you to develop the professional skills that are critical for a successful career in the financial services. \n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Accounting and Finance MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-BS%2FA%26F)\n#### Year 1 compulsory modules\nModule Name | Credits  \n---|---  \nModule Name  Quantitative Methods  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Corporate Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Accounting and Organisational Performance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Applied Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Advanced Financial Reporting  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Accounting and Finance Dissertation  |  Credits  60   \nModule Name  Critical Skills for the Finance Professional  |  Credits  15   \n#### Year 1 optional modules (selection of typical options shown below)\nModule Name | Credits  \n---|---  \nModule Name  Information and Organisation Design  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  International Business Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Forensic Accounting and Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Behavioural Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  International Investment  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  International Banking and Finance  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Python Programming for Finance  |  Credits  15   \n### Learning and teaching\nYou’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. The rest of your time will be spent in independent learning, allowing you to develop your skills in research and analysis.\nOur Virtual Learning Environment will help support your studies. This is a central place where you can find all the information and resources for the School, your course and modules.\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\n### Assessment\nAssessment methods emphasise both knowledge and essential skills development. This may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs. \nThis diversity enables you to develop a broad range of skills as preparation for your professional career.\n## Applying\n### Entry requirements\nA Bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent in a related subject, for example accounting, economics or finance. Must have a good grounding in quantitative subjects.\n**International qualifications**\nWe accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-equivalents-2).\n#### English language requirements\nIELTS 6.5 overall, with no less than 6.0 in any component. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").\n**Improve your English**\nInternational students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study our postgraduate pre-sessional English course, to help improve your English language level.\nThis pre-sessional course is designed with a progression route to your degree programme and you’ll learn academic English in the context of your subject area. To find out more, read [Language for Business (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k022/language-for-business-6-weeks- "Language for Marketing 6 weeks") and [Language for Business (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/k023/language-for-business-10-weeks- "Language for Business: Marketing \\(10 weeks\\)").\nWe also offer online pre-sessionals alongside our on-campus pre-sessionals. Find out more about our [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-) and our [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-). \nYou can also study pre-sessionals for longer periods – read about our [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).\n### How to apply\n**Documents and information you\'ll need**\n  * a copy of your degree certificate and transcript, or a partial transcript if you’re still studying \n  * contact details for two academic references \n  * a personal statement \n  * an up-to-date CV \n  * your approved English Language test* (if applicable)\n  * a letter of sponsorship, if you need one. \n\n\n* Applicants who have not yet completed an [approved English language test](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/entry-requirements/english-language-requirements/) may apply for a Masters course prior to taking a test.\nRead about visas, immigration and other information in [International students](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/international/ "International students"). We recommend that international students apply as early as possible to ensure that they have time to apply for their visa.\n### Admissions policy\n[University of Leeds Admissions Policy 2026](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/study/doc/university-leeds-admissions-policy-2026-27)\n### This course is taught by\n[Leeds University Business School](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/%20)\n### Contact us\nPostgraduate Admissions Office\nEmail: masters@lubs.leeds.ac.uk  \nTelephone: \n## Fees\nUK: £18,750 (Total)\nInternational: £35,500 (Total)\nRead more about [paying fees and charges](https://students.leeds.ac.uk/pay-fees "paying fees and charges").\nFor fees information for international taught postgraduate students, read [Masters fees](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/pgtfees/).\n### Additional cost information\nThere may be additional costs related to your course or programme of study, or related to being a student at the University of Leeds. You’ll develop strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, alongside in-demand skills, including: \n  * financial reporting standards \n  * performance evaluation \n  * capital management \n  * quantitative skills such as financial modelling and analytics \n  * technical accounting expertise \n  * problem-solving and strategic decision-making \n  * leadership and teamworking \n  * commercial and ethical awareness \n  * digital literacy \n  * presentation and written communication skills \n  * enterprise acumen \n  * sustainability awareness. \n\n\nAs part of our dedicated Critical Skills module, you’ll take part in a Professional Experience Week where you can test your skills in a supported environment. You’ll identify problems, analyse financial and non-financial data, and exercise your professional and ethical judgement to develop real-world recommendations. \n#### Where this degree could take you \nCareer opportunities for graduates of this course are vast, with recent graduates working as: \n  * audit managers – such as group audit managers and tax audit managers \n  * finance managers – for example, financial reporting managers, capital finance managers and treasury accounting managers \n  * management consultants – such as accounting advisory consultants, cost optimisation consultants and tax advisory consultants \n  * forensic accountants – including forensic auditors, financial crime analysts, and fraud examiners/investigators. \n\n\nThis course prepares you for a global financial career, and graduates have secured roles in companies such as Barclays, BDO, CCB, China UnionPay International, Deloitte, EY, HSBC, Inditex, KPMG, Lloyds Banking Group, PwC and Virgin Media O2. \nThis masters is also an excellent qualification for individuals seeking to pursue a [postgraduate research degree](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-degrees). \n> _“My experience at Leeds University Business School has been spectacular. As a postgraduate student, I have the opportunity to use facilities that enhance my academic experience, such as collaborative teaching spaces, which means I can interact with my lecturers and work with my fellow students using digital technology. My course has a lot of variety, and includes workshops, practical assignments and presentations, which have all developed my confidence.”_\n> _[Anam Tahir, MSC Accounting and Finance](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/finance/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/1551/anam-tahir?searchDirCategoryID=10007) _\nLearn more about the careers our students have pursued – read alumni profiles from [Leeds University Business School](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/finance/dir/student-alumni-profiles?query=&categoryID=185&searchDirCategoryID=10007).\n#### Top 10 most targeted for 10+ years\nby the UK\'s leading employers\n[The Graduate Market 2026, High Fliers Research](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/1057082063/)\n### Careers support\nAt Leeds, we help you to prepare for your future from day one.\nOur [Careers Service](https://students.leeds.ac.uk/) has the global expertise and sector-spanning industry partnerships that, combined, go way beyond simply helping you get a job. They provide you with the resources you need to upskill and achieve the future you aspire towards – even in the face of lightning-paced change.\n  * Dedicated Employability Team – meet with our qualified careers consultants and specialist employability and placements officers, on hand to help you choose the right path and develop the skills to get there. They can support with CV and cover letter writing, LinkedIn profile building, mock interviews and navigating AI: get confident with tailored advice and techniques.\n  * Employability and networking events – get involved in a full range of events, including careers fairs and specialist industry talks with employers who are actively recruiting. You’ll also benefit from mentoring and a supportive careers community, helping you make connections, build your network, and shape your journey as a future professional.\n  * Skills training – we embed transferable skills training in all our programmes to support your transition to the workplace. Gain expertise employers value, such as communication, problem-solving and research and data analysis.\n  * MyCareer system —– access a dedicated portal where you can book careers appointments, view helpful resources and browse vacancies and events. Access digital tools, including LinkedIn support, video‑interview preparation, plus global job market and visa guidance. We also offer pre‑arrival support to help you prepare for career planning in the UK and make the most of your time with us.\n  * Exclusive opportunities – bring your enterprise to market with our award-winning business advice service, [Spark](https://students.leeds.ac.uk/spark). Apply for vacancies only available to our students. And hone your skills further with Leeds University Union, home to volunteering opportunities and over 300 clubs and societies.\n\n\nExplore more about your employability opportunities at the University of Leeds.\n#### Study abroad tours \nAll Leeds University Business School Masters students can apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbusiness.leeds.ac.uk%2Fmasters%2Fdoc%2Finternational-study-tour-2&data=05%7C02%7CJ.H.Neary%40leeds.ac.uk%7Ca556d137a1aa4b17380108dca5ad3ca4%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638567410667728266%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=A2qg6C57v7IxUXudS6PCv35kZTyb%2Bl0KrxQSlvJtaRU%3D&reserved=0), which includes company visits, guest lectures and networking events. Previous study tours have included visits to Berlin, Frankfurt, Milan and Zurich. \n#### Links with industry \nAs a student of the Accounting and Finance Department, you can benefit from commercial awareness networking events and guest lectures from high-profile industry speakers or regulatory bodies. In addition, you\'ll experience an intensive five-day trading bootcamp with [Amplify ME](https://amplifyme.com/) – an interactive, real-world learning experience with immersive simulations of various financial services sector roles. \n#### Guaranteed industry experience \nThe Global Industry Programme gives Masters students a great opportunity to gain real-world experience through live industry projects. You’ll connect with leading companies across the globe to work on impactful, hands-on consultancy projects, enhancing your employability skills and enabling you to apply your theoretical knowledge to practical business challenges. \n## [Find out more](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/masters-your-career/doc/industry-experience-boost-career)\n## Work placements and industry experience\nAs a Masters student at Leeds, you’ll have the unique opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with our Global Industry Programme.\nYou’ll develop key professional skills and gain invaluable insight into working in your chosen field, helping to solve a real business problem from a live company brief.\nThis experience will enhance your CV, helping you to stand out in the competitive graduate jobs market and improving your chances of securing the career you want.\nBenefits of the Global Industry Programme:\n  * Fully online and designed to fit around your studies.\n  * Opportunities to make professional networks in areas such as digital marketing, business growth, sustainability and funding strategy.\n  * Gain valuable insight and build consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation, working on a time limited brief.\n  * Work as part of a team across disciplines to tackle real business needs.\n  * Advance your experience and hands-on skills by putting the course teachings into practice.\n  * Improve your employability prospects.\n  * Make new friends, build confidence and consider your future plans.\n\n\n## [Find out information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Student doing a nuclear engineering experiment in the lab](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Advanced_Chemical_Engineering_800_x_260.png)\nThis course has been specifically designed to provide greater depth in aspects of advanced chemical engineering and a range of up-to-date process technologies. These will enable you to design, operate and manage processes and associated manufacturing plants, whilst providing leadership in innovation, research and development and technology transfer.\nYou’ll study in the School of Chemical and Process Engineering which is actively involved in [‘internationally excellent’ research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-research-innovation) that has impacted the world. This gives us first-hand insight into the latest trends and practices in modern chemical engineering — much of which is fed directly into the course.\nThis means that, once you graduate, you’ll be fully equipped with the forward-thinking, relevant and topical knowledge sought after by global companies in industry. Plus, your extensive skill set will open the door to many different career paths — including developing sustainable chemical products, functional materials and pharmaceuticals, and their manufacturing processes.\nDuring your studies, you’ll also have access to specialist facilities that will complement your curriculum requirements and be taught by expert lecturers who are leaders in their fields.\n### **Why study at Leeds:**\n  * This Masters degree is accredited by the Institution of Chemical Engineers (IChemE).\n  * Our [globally-renowned research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-research-innovation) conducted right here in our School feeds into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in areas such as sustainable systems and processes.\n  * Advance your knowledge and skills in critical areas sought after in industry such as reaction engineering, multi-scale modelling and product design and development.\n  * Tailor the course to specialise in your career interests through a variety of optional modules including energy management and conservation, fuel processing and nanomaterials.\n  * Conduct your own individual research project as part of your course and gain industry experience in planning, executing and reporting.\n  * Access UK-leading [research laboratories and specialist facilities](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-undergraduate/doc/chemical-engineering-facilities), including Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Discrete Element Method (DEM) for modelling and simulation of a wide range of processes and facilities for particle science and engineering, nanotechnology and colloid science and technology.\n  * Experience excellent practical and theoretical teaching delivered by a programme team with a wealth of expertise and experience across many chemical and process engineering disciplines.\n  * Enhance your career prospects and become part of our successful alumni who have pursued exciting careers in global companies including P&G, Pfizer, Syngenta and Origin Energy.\n  * Master the most up-to-date practices and techniques recognised in industry on a course that has been directly informed and advised by the [Industrial Advisory Board](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-masters/doc/industrial-advisory-board-1).\n\n\n### **Guaranteed Work Experience**\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. \nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree—enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market. \n## [Find out more](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n### Accreditation\nAccreditation is the assurance that a university course meets the quality standards established by the profession for which it prepares its students.\nThis course is accredited by the [Institution of Chemical Engineers](https://www.icheme.org/) (IChemE) on behalf of the [Engineering Council](https://www.engc.org.uk/).\nThis Masters degree is accredited as meeting the requirements for Further Learning to Masters Level if you have an IChemE-accredited bachelor\'s degree (or have the academic equivalent assessed through the IChemE Individual Case Procedure). This provides the fast-track route to professional Chartered Engineer (CEng) status and ensures the quality of the education provided.\n![Institution of Chemical Engineers \\(IChemE\\)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/Institution_of_Chemical_Engineers_min.jpg)\n[Institution of Chemical Engineers (IChemE)](http://www.icheme.org/)\n## Course details and modules\nThe compulsory modules on the course include industry-relevant topics surrounding smarter product development through the digitalisation of processes. This includes recent advances in chemical engineering, multi-scale modelling and simulation (including CFD and DEM), advanced reaction engineering and product design and development. Alongside the core modules, you’ll also have a choice of optional modules, as well as research project topics, allowing you to gain specialist knowledge in a topic that suits your career plans or personal interests. Optional module topics include energy management and conservation, fuel processing and nanomaterials. \n### **Course structure**\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### **Compulsory modules**\n**Chemical Products Design and Development – 15 credits**\nThis module introduces the challenges faced in bringing a new product to market. Basic skills, linking product benefits and performance to market need, will be developed along with aspects of new product design and the selection processes needed to refine a concept.\n**Multi-Scale Modelling and Simulation – 30 credits**\nYou\'ll be provided with an overview of modelling techniques at the microscopic, mesoscopic and macroscopic length scales, e.g. molecular modelling, discrete element methods, computational fluid dynamics and process systems modelling. You’ll cover how multi-scale modelling can be applied to solve practical problems via a number of case studies.\n**Advanced Reaction Engineering – 15 credits**\nThis module covers advanced topics in reaction engineering, including non-isothermal operation and stability of reactors, non-ideal flow reactors, reactions catalysed by solids and design of packed and fluidised bed reactors, multi-phase reactions and reactor design, and recent advances in reaction engineering.\n**Advances in Chemical Engineering – 15 credits**\nThis module introduces the most recent developments in chemical engineering science and technology, covering topics such digital process design and manufacturing, sustainable chemical processes and advanced materials.\n**Research Project (MSc) – 60 credits**\nEvery student undertakes a research project that runs throughout the latter part of the year. This project allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests. \nThroughout the research project, you’ll work alongside PhD students and experienced researchers developing an innovative, independent piece of work, reflecting the knowledge and skills you’ve acquired. This will enable you to gain experience of planning, executing and reporting research work of the type you’ll undertake in an industrial or academic environment. information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Student doing a nuclear engineering experiment in the lab](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Advanced_Chemical_Engineering_800_x_260.png)\nThis course has been specifically designed to provide greater depth in aspects of advanced chemical engineering and a range of up-to-date process technologies. These will enable you to design, operate and manage processes and associated manufacturing plants, whilst providing leadership in innovation, research and development and technology transfer.\nYou’ll study in the School of Chemical and Process Engineering which is actively involved in [‘internationally excellent’ research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-research-innovation) that has impacted the world. This gives us first-hand insight into the latest trends and practices in modern chemical engineering — much of which is fed directly into the course.\nThis means that, once you graduate, you’ll be fully equipped with the forward-thinking, relevant and topical knowledge sought after by global companies in industry. Plus, your extensive skill set will open the door to many different career paths — including developing sustainable chemical products, functional materials and pharmaceuticals, and their manufacturing processes.\nDuring your studies, you’ll also have access to specialist facilities that will complement your curriculum requirements and be taught by expert lecturers who are leaders in their fields.\n### **Why study at Leeds:**\n  * This Masters degree is accredited by the Institution of Chemical Engineers (IChemE).\n  * Our [globally-renowned research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-research-innovation) conducted right here in our School feeds into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in areas such as sustainable systems and processes.\n  * Advance your knowledge and skills in critical areas sought after in industry such as reaction engineering, multi-scale modelling and product design and development.\n  * Tailor the course to specialise in your career interests through a variety of optional modules including energy management and conservation, fuel processing and nanomaterials.\n  * Conduct your own individual research project as part of your course and gain industry experience in planning, executing and reporting.\n  * Access UK-leading [research laboratories and specialist facilities](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-undergraduate/doc/chemical-engineering-facilities), including Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Discrete Element Method (DEM) for modelling and simulation of a wide range of processes and facilities for particle science and engineering, nanotechnology and colloid science and technology.\n  * Experience excellent practical and theoretical teaching delivered by a programme team with a wealth of expertise and experience across many chemical and process engineering disciplines.\n  * Enhance your career prospects and become part of our successful alumni who have pursued exciting careers in global companies including P&G, Pfizer, Syngenta and Origin Energy.\n  * Master the most up-to-date practices and techniques recognised in industry on a course that has been directly informed and advised by the [Industrial Advisory Board](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-masters/doc/industrial-advisory-board-1).\n\n\n### **Guaranteed Work Experience**\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. \nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree—enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market. \n## [Find out more](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n### Accreditation\nAccreditation is the assurance that a university course meets the quality standards established by the profession for which it prepares its students.\nThis course is accredited by the [Institution of Chemical Engineers](https://www.icheme.org/) (IChemE) on behalf of the [Engineering Council](https://www.engc.org.uk/).\nThis Masters degree is accredited as meeting the requirements for Further Learning to Masters Level if you have an IChemE-accredited bachelor\'s degree (or have the academic equivalent assessed through the IChemE Individual Case Procedure). This provides the fast-track route to professional Chartered Engineer (CEng) status and ensures the quality of the education provided.\n![Institution of Chemical Engineers \\(IChemE\\)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/Institution_of_Chemical_Engineers_min.jpg)\n[Institution of Chemical Engineers (IChemE)](http://www.icheme.org/)\n## Course details and modules\nThe compulsory modules on the course include industry-relevant topics surrounding smarter product development through the digitalisation of processes. This includes recent advances in chemical engineering, multi-scale modelling and simulation (including CFD and DEM), advanced reaction engineering and product design and development. Alongside the core modules, you’ll also have a choice of optional modules, as well as research project topics, allowing you to gain specialist knowledge in a topic that suits your career plans or personal interests. Optional module topics include energy management and conservation, fuel processing and nanomaterials. \n### **Course structure**\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### **Compulsory modules**\n**Chemical Products Design and Development – 15 credits**\nThis module introduces the challenges faced in bringing a new product to market. Basic skills, linking product benefits and performance to market need, will be developed along with aspects of new product design and the selection processes needed to refine a concept.\n**Multi-Scale Modelling and Simulation – 30 credits**\nYou\'ll be provided with an overview of modelling techniques at the microscopic, mesoscopic and macroscopic length scales, e.g. molecular modelling, discrete element methods, computational fluid dynamics and process systems modelling. You’ll cover how multi-scale modelling can be applied to solve practical problems via a number of case studies.\n**Advanced Reaction Engineering – 15 credits**\nThis module covers advanced topics in reaction engineering, including non-isothermal operation and stability of reactors, non-ideal flow reactors, reactions catalysed by solids and design of packed and fluidised bed reactors, multi-phase reactions and reactor design, and recent advances in reaction engineering.\n**Advances in Chemical Engineering – 15 credits**\nThis module introduces the most recent developments in chemical engineering science and technology, covering topics such digital process design and manufacturing, sustainable chemical processes and advanced materials.\n**Research Project (MSc) – 60 credits**\nEvery student undertakes a research project that runs throughout the latter part of the year. This project allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests. \nThroughout the research project, you’ll work alongside PhD students and experienced researchers developing an innovative, independent piece of work, reflecting the knowledge and skills you’ve acquired. This will enable you to gain experience of planning, executing and reporting research work of the type you’ll undertake in an industrial or academic environment. You’ll also have access to some of the outstanding facilities in the School of Chemical and Process Engineering. \nSome projects may be formally linked to industry and may include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer. \n#### **Optional modules**\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Biorefining and Future Fuels – 15 credits**\nYou’ll explore how modern oil refineries for marine, road, and aviation fuels are transforming into bio-refineries producing sustainable and future fuels. You’ll learn about conventional refinery processes, 1st–3rd generation biofuels, emerging technologies, and new bio-refinery concepts. You’ll cover process descriptions, numerical methods, health and safety, and environmental impacts. \n**Carbon and Energy Management – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll gain the knowledge and skills to manage and control carbon and greenhouse gas emissions, and to improve energy use and efficiency in industrial and commercial settings. You’ll learn approaches relevant to helping organisations meet increasingly strict emissions regulations, including aspects of ISO 14001. \n**Energy Production Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a theoretical and practical introduction to the clean energy production technologies: wind, solar, hydro, tidal and wave. Global energy production trends and the relevant readiness level of novel technologies is also covered. This module includes laboratory sessions for selected technologies. \n**Materials Structures and Characterisation – 15 credits**\nThis module provides an understanding of the range of techniques available to investigate the morphology, structure and chemistry of materials and how these link into resultant materials properties. \n**Nanomaterials – 15 credits**\nYou\'ll be provided with an understanding of the properties and processing of inorganic nanomaterials, nanoparticles and thin films and how this leads to their potential applications in electronic, biomedical and structural applications. \n**Ceramics, Polymers and Composites – 15 credits**\nThis module covers the design of conventional and advanced ceramics, polymers and composite materials. \n### **Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language**\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738105214%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=IHltoP5U3GSuosMGs97gnbuKzLMHk%2FsYilWpKj1rIH4%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary. \nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies. \n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Chemical Engineering MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-CEM%2FACE)\n### Learning and teaching\nWe use a variety of teaching and learning methods including lectures, practicals, tutorials and seminars. Independent study is also an important element of the course, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### **Specialist facilities**\nWe have [UK-leading facilities](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/chemical-engineering-masters/doc/chemical-engineering-facilities) for carrying out research in manufacturing (including crystallisation and spray drying), processing and characterising particulate systems for a wide range of technological materials, as well as facilities for nanotechnology and colloid engineering. \nWe also have high-performance computing facilities and state-of-the-art computer software, including molecular modelling, CFD, DEM and AspenHYSYS, for modelling and simulation of a wide range of processes. This provides students with strong background knowledge in industrial process and equipment design and optimisation. Our IT network gives our students on- and off-campus online access to advanced software through yearly renewed licenses, allowing you to connect with state-of-the-art tools for modelling, data processing and predictive simulations. \nOur comprehensive catalogue of online subscriptions to science and engineering journals provides you with the latest advances as well as historical research. \n#### **Programme team**\nOur programme team combines world-class academic expertise with real-world industry insight. You’ll be taught by leading academics, from innovative lecturers to internationally recognised professors, whose research is shaping the future of chemical and process engineering. Experienced industry professionals will share practical knowledge from the field, while our trained postgraduate researchers bring fresh perspectives from the cutting edge of discovery. Together, they’ll connect you to a vibrant network of expertise and opportunity. \nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\n### Assessment\nYou’ll be assessed using a range of techniques including problem sheets, technical reports, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessments.\n## Applying\n### Entry requirements\nA bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in chemical engineering or similar (e.g. chemical engineering and technology, chemical and process engineering, or mechanical engineering). \nAlternative subjects which may be considered include, but are not limited to, petroleum engineering, energy engineering, energy and power engineering, civil engineering or polymer engineering. All applicants must have strong marks across a breadth of relevant modules, including mathematics and engineering fundamentals. \nApplicants with a 2:2 (hons) will be considered on a case-by-case basis where they can demonstrate competence in specific core chemical engineering modules and/or with relevant professional qualifications or experience. \nWe accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications). experienced, registered health and care practitioners to a level of practice characterised by a high degree of autonomy and complex decision making. This master’s level award encompasses the four pillars of clinical practice:\\n  * Clinical practice.\\n  * Leadership and management.\\n  * Education.\\n  * Research.\\n\\n\\nAdvanced Clinical Practice embodies the ability to manage clinical care in partnership with individuals, families and carers. It includes the analysis and synthesis of complex problems across a range of settings, enabling innovative solutions to enhance people’s healthcare experience and improve outcomes. Practitioners will also be able to demonstrate core capabilities and area specific clinical competence.\\nThe aim of this programme is to provide healthcare practitioners with the knowledge and skills for advanced clinical practice that will enable them to function competently in:\\n  * Providing effective healthcare.\\n  * Improving the quality and health outcomes.\\n  * Evaluation and research.\\n  * Leading and developing practice.\\n  * Developing self and others.\\n  * Working across professional and organisational boundaries.\\n  * Innovation and changing practice.\\n\\n\\nThe School of Healthcare is one of the largest multi-professional health schools in the country. You’ll have the opportunity to study in a research-intensive university, alongside those with whom you’ll work in clinical practice.\\nThe programme leader is Ian Goulden: i.goulden@leeds.ac.uk\\n## Course details and modules\\nThe Masters in Advanced Clinical Practice course has three compulsory modules focusing on advancing practice, innovation and research. The programme will comprise 75 compulsory credits and 105 optional credits. The programme should be completed in two to three years.\\nOptional modules are focused on developing knowledge and skills for advanced clinical practice.\\nN.B. Related content\n###  [Course Terms and Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Healthcare professionals walking down a hospital corridor.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Untitled_design__1_.png)\nThis programme is for experienced practitioners, such as nurses, pharmacists, radiographers, audiologists, cardiac physiologists, ambulance staff and midwives, who have clinical practice access with patient management responsibilities.\nIt’s designed to support the development of experienced, registered health and care practitioners to a level of practice characterised by a high degree of autonomy and complex decision making. This master’s level award encompasses the four pillars of clinical practice:\n  * Clinical practice.\n  * Leadership and management.\n  * Education.\n  * Research.\n\n\nAdvanced Clinical Practice embodies the ability to manage clinical care in partnership with individuals, families and carers. It includes the analysis and synthesis of complex problems across a range of settings, enabling innovative solutions to enhance people’s healthcare experience and improve outcomes. Practitioners will also be able to demonstrate core capabilities and area specific clinical competence.\nThe aim of this programme is to provide healthcare practitioners with the knowledge and skills for advanced clinical practice that will enable them to function competently in:\n  * Providing effective healthcare.\n  * Improving the quality and health outcomes.\n  * Evaluation and research.\n  * Leading and developing practice.\n  * Developing self and others.\n  * Working across professional and organisational boundaries.\n  * Innovation and changing practice.\n\n\nThe School of Healthcare is one of the largest multi-professional health schools in the country. You’ll have the opportunity to study in a research-intensive university, alongside those with whom you’ll work in clinical practice.\nThe programme leader is Ian Goulden: i.goulden@leeds.ac.uk\n## Course details and modules\nThe Masters in Advanced Clinical Practice course has three compulsory modules focusing on advancing practice, innovation and research. The programme will comprise 75 compulsory credits and 105 optional credits. The programme should be completed in two to three years.\nOptional modules are focused on developing knowledge and skills for advanced clinical practice.\nN.B. Some modules may not deliver every year, and some may have specific entry criteria.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Clinical Practice MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ADCP-18S)\n#### Year 2 compulsory modules\nModule Name | Credits  \n---|---  \nModule Name  Issues and Concepts of Advancing Practice  |  Credits  15   \nModule Name  Advanced Practitioner Inquiry  |  Credits  45   \nModule Name  Research Methods  |  Credits  15   \n### Learning and teaching\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\n### Assessment\nThe programme aims to keep the assessment load at a manageable level whilst ensuring that students are adequately prepared for the role. As such whenever possible, assessment methods will support day to day practice and will test/exam practice applicable knowledge and skills. The aim is for the assessment to be of use within the workplace as well as providing evidence that you have achieved the learning outcomes for the module.\nA range of assessment methods are used in the various modules that will make up this programme. Assessments will depend to a large extent on the optional modules selected. Alongside the academic components of the programme you will complete an e-portfolio to confirm achievement of the required ACP knowledge. skills and behaviours.\n## Applying\n### Entry requirements\nApplicants must:\n  * Be a currently practising registered healthcare practitioner.\n  * Hold a degree in a health-related discipline. Normally this will be an Honours degree at 2:1 classification or above. However individual consideration will be given to suitable applicants who do not have an Honours degree or who do not have a 2:1 classification).\n  * Be in employment as a trainee advanced clinical practitioner or be in a role in which the programme outcomes can be achieved (please contact the programme leader for advice).\n  * Have a satisfactory application and interview.\n\n\n**Student selection**\nEligible students will be interviewed either as part of their employer’s recruitment process or separately within the University.\n#### English language requirements\n**Improve your English**\nInternational students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study our postgraduate pre-sessional English course, to help improve your English language level.\nThis pre-sessional course is designed with a progression route to your degree programme and you’ll learn academic English in the context of your subject area. responsibilities.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-LauraOmand.jpg)\\nThis programme is for experienced health and social care practitioners who are either currently working in an advanced clinical practice role or who have obtained a trainee advanced clinical practitioner role prior to starting the programme. The course is designed to support your development under the four pillars of advanced practice:\\n  * Clinical practice.\\n  * Leadership and Management.\\n  * Education.\\n  * Research.\\n\\n\\nAdvanced clinical practice embodies the ability to manage clinical care in partnership with individuals, families and carers. It includes the analysis and synthesis of complex problems across a range of settings, enabling innovative solutions to enhance people’s healthcare experience and improve outcomes. You’ll be required to demonstrate core capabilities and area specific clinical competence.\\nThe School of Healthcare is one of the largest multi-professional health schools in the country. You’ll have the opportunity to study in a research-intensive university, alongside those with whom you’ll work in clinical practice.\\nThe programme leader is Ian Goulden: i.goulden@leeds.ac.uk.\\nPlease note: you must either be already working as an Advanced Clinical Practitioner or must have secured a trainee Advanced Clinical practitioner role prior to application.\\n## Course details and modules\\nThe MSc Advanced Clinical Practice – Apprenticeship has four compulsory modules (75 credits in total) and 105 optional module credits.\\nThe optional modules are designed to enable you to focus your learning on your own particular care environment whilst maintaining the fundamental components of advanced clinical practice. The programme is designed to be studied over three years.\\n### Course structure\\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Clinical Practice (Apprenticeship) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-APACP-20)\\n#### Year 1 compulsory modules\\nModule Name | Credits  \\n---|---  \\nModule Name  Issues and Concepts of Advancing Practice  |  Credits  15   \\nModule Name  Research Methods  |  Credits  15   \\n#### Year 2 compulsory modules\\nModule Name | Credits  \\n---|---  \\nModule Name  Issues and Concepts of Advancing Practice  |  Credits  15   \\nModule Name  Research Methods  |  Credits  15   \\n#### Year 3 compulsory modules\\nModule Name | Credits  \\n---|---  \\nModule Name  Advanced Practitioner Inquiry (Apprenticeship)  |  Credits  25   \\nModule Name  Advanced Clinical Practice End Point Assessment  |  Credits  20   \\n### Learning and teaching\\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\\n### Assessment\\nThe programme aims to keep the assessment load at a manageable level whilst ensuring that you are adequately prepared for the role. As such, whenever possible, assessment methods will support day to day practice and will test practice applicable knowledge and skills. The aim is for the assessment to be of use within the workplace as well as providing evidence that you’ve achieved the learning outcomes for the module. \\nA range of assessment methods are used in the various modules that will make up this programme. The type of assessment will depend to a large extent on the optional modules selected. \\nIn addition to the module assessments, you’ll be required to complete a range of core clinical competencies as well as specific ones determined by your employer. \\n## Applying\\n### Entry requirements\\nYou must: \\n  * Be currently registered with an appropriate health / social care professional body. \\n  * Possess a degree in a health / social care related discipline from a recognised higher education institution. (Normally this will be an Honours degree at 2:1 classification or above. However, consideration will be given to suitable applicants who do not have an Honours degree or who do not have a 2:1 classification.) \\n  * Be working in an advanced practice role or as a trainee advanced clinical practitioner at the start of and throughout the programme. \\n  * Have a satisfactory application and interview. \\n\\n\\nIn addition, prior to being submitted for the End Point Assessment, students will be required to show that they have achieved GCSE English Language / English Literature and Mathematics at grade 4 or above (or grade C or above if awarded under the previous GCSE grading scheme), or have achieved Level 2 Functional Skills in English and Mathematics (or any agreed equivalencies). \\nIndividuals are eligible for apprenticeship funding through an employer’s apprenticeship service account or government-employer co-investment if they have a valid and eligible residency status. Non-UK nationals are eligible for funding if they have permission from the UK government to live in the UK (not for educational purposes), and have been ordinarily resident in the UK for at least the previous three years before the start of the apprenticeship. Related content\n###  [Course Terms and Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Three students sat at a table, one student is holding a hexapod, a 6 legged robot. To the back of the table there is a open laptop displaying code that runs the robot.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260_5.jpg)\n**Take your computing skills to the next level and master the latest technologies that are innovating almost every industry.**\nComputing is integral to our society. That’s why qualified specialists in this field are highly sought after by many different industries. \nOur Advanced Computer Science MSc is wide-ranging, exploring advanced topics in computer science, which will equip you with the understanding and practical skills to succeed in a variety of careers. \nBuilding on your existing knowledge of computer science, you’ll really hone your skills and expertise in designing and implementing larger, more complex systems using state-of-the-art technologies. \nYou’ll even have the chance to work as an integral member of one of our research groups when you develop your main project. \nFrom AI to cybersecurity, data science to software development, this MSc will open you up to a range of high-demand technical roles across multiple industries. \n> _“There are so many great opportunities at university, especially at Leeds, that you’ll never get elsewhere. You will learn so many skills on the course, but make sure to delve into the other opportunities at university and across Leeds. Make the most of living in the best city in the UK!”  \n> [Ben Swift, Advanced Computer Science MSc](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/4379/ben-swift) _\n### Why study at Leeds \n  * [**Globally-renowned research** :](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) This feeds directly into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in everything from AI to biomedicine, algorithms to computational engineering – and beyond. \n  * **Unique professional partnership** s: Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and AI. \n  * **Tailor your degree** : Choose from a wide range of optional modules to suit your specific interests, such as data science, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning and advanced software engineering. \n  * **Build real-world industry experience** : Conduct your own individual project, which focuses on an industry-led topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking. \n  * **Access industry-standard specialist facilities:** You\'ll get to use our state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a robotics lab with a range of equipment available for specialist MSc projects. [Take a virtual tour](https://explore.leeds.ac.uk/). \n  * **Bring your skills to life outside the classroom** : Our extra-curricular activities include a 24-hour hackathon backed by industry sponsors and [CompSoc](https://engage.luu.org.uk/groups/PQ3/leeds-computing-society-compsoc), a hands-on integrated design project, the [UKIEPC national programming competition](https://ukiepc.info/) hosted on campus, building a rocket with the [Leeds University Rocketry Association](https://leedsrocketry.co.uk/) or attending the [British Computing Society’s Women Lovelace Colloquium](https://bcswomenlovelace.bcs.org/). \n\n\n#### Guaranteed Work Experience \nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience programme](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. \nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree — enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market. \n## [Learn more about the programme](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/f753/eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n## Course details and modules\nIn the first half of the year, you’ll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of algorithms and systems programming.\nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as cloud computing, blockchain technologies, machine learning, data mining and text analytics.\nDuring the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**MSc Project – 60 credits**\nYou’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests.\nRecent examples include:\n  * iPad interaction for wall-sized displays\n  * Modelling the effects of feature-based attention in the visual cortex\n  * Energy-efficient cloud computing.\n\n\nA proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Bio-inspired Computing – 15 credits**\nDuring this module, you’ll learn to interpret the behaviour of algorithms based on the cooperative behaviour of distributed agents with no, or little, central control, plus implement bio-inspired algorithms to solve a range of problems.\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nDuring this module you’ll analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages and get to grips with automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module covers topics including neural networks, decision trees, support vector machines, Bayesian learning, instance-based learning, linear regression, clustering, reinforcement learning, deep learning and methods for evaluating performance.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module gives you the opportunity to understand and use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems. You’ll develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits, and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n**Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**\nGraphs are an extremely powerful tool for modelling real-world systems, with applications in logistics, telecommunication, molecular biology, industrial engineering, linguistics, chemistry, and many other areas. Many of the optimisation problems arising from these applications are computationally difficult when there are no restrictions on the input. However, the scenarios that we aim to model often impose additional conditions on the structure of the corresponding graphs. This module focuses on how that structural information can be used to solve the relevant optimisation problems efficiently, with an emphasis on mathematical precision.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS-FT)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines, through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings.\nIndependent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### Specialist facilities\nAt Leeds, we provide an exciting environment in which to gain a range of skills and experience cutting-edge technology.\nYou’ll benefit from UK-leading facilities to support your learning, including:\n  * A state-of-the art computing cluster, equipped with Azure services and a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker\n  * Individual machines, equipped with Microsoft- or Linux-software, capable of performing rendering\n  * Robotics labs\n  * Dedicated Linux laboratories with a combined capacity of an average of 150 machines\n  * Excellent facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building.
