Related content\n###  [Course Terms and Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Three students sat at a table, one student is holding a hexapod, a 6 legged robot. To the back of the table there is a open laptop displaying code that runs the robot.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260_5.jpg)\n**Take your computing skills to the next level and master the latest technologies that are innovating almost every industry.**\nComputing is integral to our society. That’s why qualified specialists in this field are highly sought after by many different industries. \nOur Advanced Computer Science MSc is wide-ranging, exploring advanced topics in computer science, which will equip you with the understanding and practical skills to succeed in a variety of careers. \nBuilding on your existing knowledge of computer science, you’ll really hone your skills and expertise in designing and implementing larger, more complex systems using state-of-the-art technologies. \nYou’ll even have the chance to work as an integral member of one of our research groups when you develop your main project. \nFrom AI to cybersecurity, data science to software development, this MSc will open you up to a range of high-demand technical roles across multiple industries. \n> _“There are so many great opportunities at university, especially at Leeds, that you’ll never get elsewhere. You will learn so many skills on the course, but make sure to delve into the other opportunities at university and across Leeds. Make the most of living in the best city in the UK!”  \n> [Ben Swift, Advanced Computer Science MSc](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/4379/ben-swift) _\n### Why study at Leeds \n  * [**Globally-renowned research** :](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) This feeds directly into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in everything from AI to biomedicine, algorithms to computational engineering – and beyond. \n  * **Unique professional partnership** s: Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and AI. \n  * **Tailor your degree** : Choose from a wide range of optional modules to suit your specific interests, such as data science, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning and advanced software engineering. \n  * **Build real-world industry experience** : Conduct your own individual project, which focuses on an industry-led topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking. \n  * **Access industry-standard specialist facilities:** You\'ll get to use our state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a robotics lab with a range of equipment available for specialist MSc projects. [Take a virtual tour](https://explore.leeds.ac.uk/). \n  * **Bring your skills to life outside the classroom** : Our extra-curricular activities include a 24-hour hackathon backed by industry sponsors and [CompSoc](https://engage.luu.org.uk/groups/PQ3/leeds-computing-society-compsoc), a hands-on integrated design project, the [UKIEPC national programming competition](https://ukiepc.info/) hosted on campus, building a rocket with the [Leeds University Rocketry Association](https://leedsrocketry.co.uk/) or attending the [British Computing Society’s Women Lovelace Colloquium](https://bcswomenlovelace.bcs.org/). \n\n\n#### Guaranteed Work Experience \nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience programme](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. \nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree — enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market. \n## [Learn more about the programme](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/f753/eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n## Course details and modules\nIn the first half of the year, you’ll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of algorithms and systems programming.\nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as cloud computing, blockchain technologies, machine learning, data mining and text analytics.\nDuring the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**MSc Project – 60 credits**\nYou’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests.\nRecent examples include:\n  * iPad interaction for wall-sized displays\n  * Modelling the effects of feature-based attention in the visual cortex\n  * Energy-efficient cloud computing.\n\n\nA proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Bio-inspired Computing – 15 credits**\nDuring this module, you’ll learn to interpret the behaviour of algorithms based on the cooperative behaviour of distributed agents with no, or little, central control, plus implement bio-inspired algorithms to solve a range of problems.\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nDuring this module you’ll analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages and get to grips with automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module covers topics including neural networks, decision trees, support vector machines, Bayesian learning, instance-based learning, linear regression, clustering, reinforcement learning, deep learning and methods for evaluating performance.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module gives you the opportunity to understand and use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems. You’ll develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits, and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n**Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**\nGraphs are an extremely powerful tool for modelling real-world systems, with applications in logistics, telecommunication, molecular biology, industrial engineering, linguistics, chemistry, and many other areas. Many of the optimisation problems arising from these applications are computationally difficult when there are no restrictions on the input. However, the scenarios that we aim to model often impose additional conditions on the structure of the corresponding graphs. This module focuses on how that structural information can be used to solve the relevant optimisation problems efficiently, with an emphasis on mathematical precision.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS-FT)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines, through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings.\nIndependent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### Specialist facilities\nAt Leeds, we provide an exciting environment in which to gain a range of skills and experience cutting-edge technology.\nYou’ll benefit from UK-leading facilities to support your learning, including:\n  * A state-of-the art computing cluster, equipped with Azure services and a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker\n  * Individual machines, equipped with Microsoft- or Linux-software, capable of performing rendering\n  * Robotics labs\n  * Dedicated Linux laboratories with a combined capacity of an average of 150 machines\n  * Excellent facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building. [Explore more of our facilities through our 360 virtual experience.](http://explore.leeds.ac.uk/)\n\n\n#### Programme team\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. One student is holding a small robot with wheels, while another student look at them pausing in conversation. In front of them a is an open laptop displaying code. There are two other robots on the table.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260__1__6.jpg)\n**Step into the future of intelligent technology with an MSc that empowers you to shape the next generation of AI and build technical skills that’ll help drive the breakthroughs of tomorrow.**\nFrom autonomous vehicles and adaptive networks to intelligent software that reshapes how organisations operate, AI is redefining every sector.\nThe world needs specialists who don’t just understand these systems but can push them further. That’s where you come in.\nOn this MSc, you’ll explore the full spectrum of intelligent systems – from machine learning and reasoning to image processing, language and bio‑computation.\nOur academics in the [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) are active innovators in their fields, meaning you’ll be learning the latest methods, breakthroughs and real‑world applications shaping the AI landscape right now.\nThe Sir William Henry Bragg Building will be your home as a computer science student, giving you access to a range of specialist facilities that’ll allow you to put theory into practice – and make your own discoveries.\nUltimately, you’ll graduate with the understanding and skills you’ll need to thrive in the rapidly expanding intelligent-tech sector.\n> _There are so many great opportunities at university, especially at Leeds, that you’ll never get elsewhere. You will learn so many skills on the course, but make sure to delve into the other opportunities at university and across Leeds. Make the most of living in the best city in the UK!_\n> _[Ben Swift, Advanced Computer Science MSc](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/4379/ben-swift)_\n### Why study at Leeds\n  * **[Globally-renowned research:](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) **This feeds directly into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in everything from AI to biomedicine, algorithms to computational engineering – and beyond.\n  * **Unique professional partnerships:** Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and AI.\n  * **Tailor your degree:** Choose from a wide range of optional modules to suit your specific interests, such as advanced data science, advanced software engineering and data mining.\n  * **Build real-world industry experience:** Conduct your own individual project, which focuses on an industry-led topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking.\n  * **Access industry-standard specialist facilities:** You\'ll get to use our state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High-Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a visualisation lab, including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and InterSsense InertiaCube orientation tracker. [Take a virtual tour](https://explore.leeds.ac.uk/).\n  * **Bring your skills to life outside the classroom:** Our extra-curricular activities include a 24-hour hackathon backed by industry sponsors and [CompSoc](https://engage.luu.org.uk/groups/PQ3/leeds-computing-society-compsoc), a hands-on integrated design project, the [UKIEPC national programming competition](https://ukiepc.info/) hosted on campus, building a rocket with the [Leeds University Rocketry Association](https://leedsrocketry.co.uk/) or attending the [British Computing Society’s Women Lovelace Colloquium](https://bcswomenlovelace.bcs.org/).\n\n\n#### Guaranteed Work Experience\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience programme](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company.\nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree — enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market.\n#### Study online\nWe also offer a fully online [Artificial Intelligence MSc](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/d995/artificial-intelligence-msc?utm_source=coursefinder&utm_medium=page&utm_campaign=AIonlineMSc) and [Postgraduate Certificate](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/d997/artificial-intelligence-postgraduate-certificate?utm_source=coursefinder&utm_medium=page&utm_campaign=AIonlinePGCert), covering an extensive range of AI and machine learning tools and techniques and designed for professionals seeking to develop expertise in this area.\n## Course details and modules\nThe first half of the year will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of algorithms and systems programming, as well as the basic principles of automated reasoning, machine learning and how computers can be made to represent knowledge.  \n  \nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as image analysis, cloud computing, graph theory and developing mobile apps.  \n  \nDuring the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nYou will learn how to analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages. You will gain an understanding automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nOn completion of this module, you should be able to: list the principal algorithms used in machine learning and derive their update rules; appreciate the capabilities and limitations of current approaches; evaluate the performance of machine learning algorithms; use existing implementation(s) of machine learning algorithms to explore data sets and build models.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Research Project – 60 credits**\nThe research project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests. Some projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Bio-Inspired Computing – 15 credits**\nDuring this module, you’ll consider examples of cooperative phenomena in nature and the concepts of emergence and self-organisation. On completion of this module, you’ll have: designed and applied simple genetic algorithms; interpreted the behaviour of algorithms based on the cooperative behaviour of distributed agents with no, or little, central control; and implemented bio-inspired algorithms to solve a range of problems.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module will provide you with an introduction to linguistic theory and terminology. On competition you should be able to: demonstrate an understanding and how to use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems; develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits; and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n**Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**\nGraphs are an extremely powerful tool for modelling real-world systems, with applications in logistics, telecommunication, molecular biology, industrial engineering, linguistics, chemistry, and many other areas. Many of the optimisation problems arising from these applications are computationally difficult when there are no restrictions on the input. However, the scenarios that we aim to model often impose additional conditions on the structure of the corresponding graphs. This module focuses on how that structural information can be used to solve the relevant optimisation problems efficiently, with an emphasis on mathematical precision.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FAI-F)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines. Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![Four students sat at a table. One student is holding a small robot with wheels, while another student look at them pausing in conversation. In front of them a is an open laptop displaying code. There are two other robots on the table.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260__1__6.jpg)\n**Step into the future of intelligent technology with an MSc that empowers you to shape the next generation of AI and build technical skills that’ll help drive the breakthroughs of tomorrow.**\nFrom autonomous vehicles and adaptive networks to intelligent software that reshapes how organisations operate, AI is redefining every sector.\nThe world needs specialists who don’t just understand these systems but can push them further. That’s where you come in.\nOn this MSc, you’ll explore the full spectrum of intelligent systems – from machine learning and reasoning to image processing, language and bio‑computation.\nOur academics in the [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) are active innovators in their fields, meaning you’ll be learning the latest methods, breakthroughs and real‑world applications shaping the AI landscape right now.\nThe Sir William Henry Bragg Building will be your home as a computer science student, giving you access to a range of specialist facilities that’ll allow you to put theory into practice – and make your own discoveries.\nUltimately, you’ll graduate with the understanding and skills you’ll need to thrive in the rapidly expanding intelligent-tech sector.\n> _There are so many great opportunities at university, especially at Leeds, that you’ll never get elsewhere. You will learn so many skills on the course, but make sure to delve into the other opportunities at university and across Leeds. Make the most of living in the best city in the UK!_\n> _[Ben Swift, Advanced Computer Science MSc](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing/dir-record/student-alumni-profiles/4379/ben-swift)_\n### Why study at Leeds\n  * **[Globally-renowned research:](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) **This feeds directly into your course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking in everything from AI to biomedicine, algorithms to computational engineering – and beyond.\n  * **Unique professional partnerships:** Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and AI.\n  * **Tailor your degree:** Choose from a wide range of optional modules to suit your specific interests, such as advanced data science, advanced software engineering and data mining.\n  * **Build real-world industry experience:** Conduct your own individual project, which focuses on an industry-led topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking.\n  * **Access industry-standard specialist facilities:** You\'ll get to use our state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High-Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a visualisation lab, including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and InterSsense InertiaCube orientation tracker. [Take a virtual tour](https://explore.leeds.ac.uk/).\n  * **Bring your skills to life outside the classroom:** Our extra-curricular activities include a 24-hour hackathon backed by industry sponsors and [CompSoc](https://engage.luu.org.uk/groups/PQ3/leeds-computing-society-compsoc), a hands-on integrated design project, the [UKIEPC national programming competition](https://ukiepc.info/) hosted on campus, building a rocket with the [Leeds University Rocketry Association](https://leedsrocketry.co.uk/) or attending the [British Computing Society’s Women Lovelace Colloquium](https://bcswomenlovelace.bcs.org/).\n\n\n#### Guaranteed Work Experience\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience programme](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company.\nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree — enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market.\n#### Study online\nWe also offer a fully online [Artificial Intelligence MSc](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/d995/artificial-intelligence-msc?utm_source=coursefinder&utm_medium=page&utm_campaign=AIonlineMSc) and [Postgraduate Certificate](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/d997/artificial-intelligence-postgraduate-certificate?utm_source=coursefinder&utm_medium=page&utm_campaign=AIonlinePGCert), covering an extensive range of AI and machine learning tools and techniques and designed for professionals seeking to develop expertise in this area.\n## Course details and modules\nThe first half of the year will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of algorithms and systems programming, as well as the basic principles of automated reasoning, machine learning and how computers can be made to represent knowledge.  \n  \nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as image analysis, cloud computing, graph theory and developing mobile apps.  \n  \nDuring the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nYou will learn how to analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages. You will gain an understanding automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nOn completion of this module, you should be able to: list the principal algorithms used in machine learning and derive their update rules; appreciate the capabilities and limitations of current approaches; evaluate the performance of machine learning algorithms; use existing implementation(s) of machine learning algorithms to explore data sets and build models.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Research Project – 60 credits**\nThe research project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests. Some projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Bio-Inspired Computing – 15 credits**\nDuring this module, you’ll consider examples of cooperative phenomena in nature and the concepts of emergence and self-organisation. On completion of this module, you’ll have: designed and applied simple genetic algorithms; interpreted the behaviour of algorithms based on the cooperative behaviour of distributed agents with no, or little, central control; and implemented bio-inspired algorithms to solve a range of problems.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module will provide you with an introduction to linguistic theory and terminology. On competition you should be able to: demonstrate an understanding and how to use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems; develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits; and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n**Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**\nGraphs are an extremely powerful tool for modelling real-world systems, with applications in logistics, telecommunication, molecular biology, industrial engineering, linguistics, chemistry, and many other areas. Many of the optimisation problems arising from these applications are computationally difficult when there are no restrictions on the input. However, the scenarios that we aim to model often impose additional conditions on the structure of the corresponding graphs. This module focuses on how that structural information can be used to solve the relevant optimisation problems efficiently, with an emphasis on mathematical precision.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FAI-F)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines. You’ll be taught through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings.\nIndependent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### Specialist facilities\nAt Leeds, we provide an exciting environment in which to gain a range of skills and experience cutting-edge technology.\nYou’ll benefit from UK-leading facilities to support your learning, including:\n  * A state-of-the art computing cluster, with access to Azure services and GPU computing as required by your modules \n  * High-performance graphics workstations, equipped with modern software libraries and tools for virtual reality and real time visualisation and interaction\n  * Robotics labs\n  * Dedicated Linux laboratories with a combined capacity of an average of 150 machines\n  * Excellent facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building.[Explore more of our facilities through our 360 virtual experience.](http://explore.leeds.ac.uk)\n\n\n#### Programme team\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\n### Assessment\nYou’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods.\n## Applying\n### Entry requirements\nA bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in computer science.\nWe require all applicants to have studied a breadth of relevant modules including significant programming, systems development, data structures and algorithms.\nApplicants with any of the following will be considered on a case-by-case basis:\n  * A bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in other computing-based degrees.\n  * A bachelor degree with a 2:2 (hons) in computer science, with at least three years of relevant experience.\n  * Professional qualifications and relevant experience.\n\n\n#### International\nWe accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications). Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![A photograph of two students and a academic in a computer science lab. The students are sat a desk with two different sized drones and a laptop. The academic is showing the students something on the screen. Behind them is a row of desk and computer chairs](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260__2__5.jpg)\nDevelopments in cloud computing technology are transforming the way we live and work. This Masters degree will equip you with specialist knowledge in this fast-growing field and allow you to explore a range of advanced topics in computer science.\nOur Advanced Computer Science MSc will build on your existing knowledge of computer science, giving you a foundation in topics like systems programming and algorithms, as well as specialist modules in advanced distributed systems – especially cloud techniques, technologies and applications.\nThe programme will give you the theoretical and practical skills required to design and implement larger, more complex systems using state-of-the-art technologies. You’ll even have the chance to work as an integral member of one of our research groups when you develop your main project.\nStudying in our [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) gives you access to a whole range of specialist facilities, whilst being taught by academics who are experts in their fields. We’re also responsible for producing internationally excellent research and have excellent links with the Cloud Computing industry including [Atos,](https://atos.net/) [Alibaba Cloud](https://us.alibabacloud.com/) and [Microsoft](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-gb/) meaning you’ll be learning the most up-to-date practices and techniques needed to pursue an exciting career in industry.\n#### Why study at Leeds:\n  * Research produced by the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and our School’s [globally-renowned research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) conducted right here on campus feeds directly into the course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking.\n  * Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.\n  * Advance your knowledge and skills in key areas of computing including software engineering, whilst focusing on both theory and practice so you can understand and implement cloud computing applications and architectures.\n  * Tailor the degree to suit your specific interests with a selection of optional modules to choose from such as data science, data mining, machine learning and blockchain technologies.\n  * Build industry experience by conducting your own individual project which focuses on a real-world topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking.\n  * Access a wide range of industry-standard specialist facilities including a state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker.\n  * Experience expert theoretical and practical teaching delivered by a programme team made up of academics who specialise in a wide range of computing topics.\n  * Study in the Sir William Henry Bragg building which provides excellent facilities and teaching spaces for an outstanding student experience. [Explore more of our facilities through our 360 virtual experience.](http://explore.leeds.ac.uk)\n\n\n### Guaranteed Work Experience\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company.\nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career-ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree—enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market.\n## [Find out more](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n## Course details and modules\nDuring the first half of the year, you\'ll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of software engineering and systems programming.\nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as machine learning, big data systems, and scientific computation.\nIn the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\nResearch projects include various topics such as edge computing, serverless architectures, big data, energy efficiency and resource management.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**MSc Project – 60 credits**\nYou’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests.\nRecent projects include:\n  * Intelligent services to support sensemaking\n  * Machine Learning based cloud resource scheduling\n  * Energy-aware resource management\n  * Scalable serverless workflows\n\n\nA proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nYou’ll learn how to analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages, understanding automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nOn completion of this module, you should be able to: list the principal algorithms used in machine learning and derive their update rules appreciate the capabilities and limitations of current approaches; evaluate the performance of machine learning algorithms; and use existing implementation(s) of machine learning algorithms to explore data sets and build models.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module will provide you with an introduction to linguistic theory and terminology. On competition you should be able to: demonstrate an understanding and how to use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems; develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits; and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Cloud Computing) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FC-FT)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines. You’ll have regular contact with them through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings.\nIndependent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### **Specialist facilities**\nAt Leeds, we provide an exciting environment in which to gain a range of skills and experience cutting-edge technology.\nYou’ll benefit from world-class facilities to support your learning, including:\n  * a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource consisting of several clusters which are used for all forms of predictive modelling, data analysis and simulation\n  * Access to Microsoft Azure cloud\n  * a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker\n  * Ascension Flock of Birds tracking systems, three DOF and 6DOF Phantom force feedback devices\n  * Twin Immersion Corp CyberGloves\n  * rendering cluster and labs containing both Microsoft and Linux platforms, among others.\n  * excellent facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building. Conditions](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\nFind further information in the course terms and conditions\n## Course overview\n![A photograph of two students and a academic in a computer science lab. The students are sat a desk with two different sized drones and a laptop. The academic is showing the students something on the screen. Behind them is a row of desk and computer chairs](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/images/resized/1600x520-0-0-1-80-Coursefinder_header_800x260__2__5.jpg)\nDevelopments in cloud computing technology are transforming the way we live and work. This Masters degree will equip you with specialist knowledge in this fast-growing field and allow you to explore a range of advanced topics in computer science.\nOur Advanced Computer Science MSc will build on your existing knowledge of computer science, giving you a foundation in topics like systems programming and algorithms, as well as specialist modules in advanced distributed systems – especially cloud techniques, technologies and applications.\nThe programme will give you the theoretical and practical skills required to design and implement larger, more complex systems using state-of-the-art technologies. You’ll even have the chance to work as an integral member of one of our research groups when you develop your main project.\nStudying in our [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) gives you access to a whole range of specialist facilities, whilst being taught by academics who are experts in their fields. We’re also responsible for producing internationally excellent research and have excellent links with the Cloud Computing industry including [Atos,](https://atos.net/) [Alibaba Cloud](https://us.alibabacloud.com/) and [Microsoft](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-gb/) meaning you’ll be learning the most up-to-date practices and techniques needed to pursue an exciting career in industry.\n#### Why study at Leeds:\n  * Research produced by the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and our School’s [globally-renowned research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) conducted right here on campus feeds directly into the course, shaping your learning with the latest thinking.\n  * Benefit from studying at a university that’s partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.\n  * Advance your knowledge and skills in key areas of computing including software engineering, whilst focusing on both theory and practice so you can understand and implement cloud computing applications and architectures.\n  * Tailor the degree to suit your specific interests with a selection of optional modules to choose from such as data science, data mining, machine learning and blockchain technologies.\n  * Build industry experience by conducting your own individual project which focuses on a real-world topic of your choice, giving you the chance to develop professional skills in research and critical thinking.\n  * Access a wide range of industry-standard specialist facilities including a state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource and a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker.\n  * Experience expert theoretical and practical teaching delivered by a programme team made up of academics who specialise in a wide range of computing topics.\n  * Study in the Sir William Henry Bragg building which provides excellent facilities and teaching spaces for an outstanding student experience. [Explore more of our facilities through our 360 virtual experience.](http://explore.leeds.ac.uk)\n\n\n### Guaranteed Work Experience\nWhile studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company.\nThis practical experience is highly valued by employers and helps you develop the skills needed to be career-ready. What sets us apart is that your work experience is formally integrated into your degree—enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience and stand out in today’s competitive job market.\n## [Find out more](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/work-experience)\n## Course details and modules\nDuring the first half of the year, you\'ll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of software engineering and systems programming.\nFrom there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as machine learning, big data systems, and scientific computation.\nIn the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project. This gives you the chance to work as an integral part of one of our active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting the appropriate research methods.\nResearch projects include various topics such as edge computing, serverless architectures, big data, energy efficiency and resource management.\n### Course structure\nThe list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. Read more in our [terms and conditions.](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/courseterms)\n#### Compulsory modules\n**Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**\nThe module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets. This module is supported by the strong research interest and expertise in cloud and related technologies within the School of Computer Science. You’ll develop expertise in cloud computing and big data systems as you’re taught the skills and knowledge to design, build and extend the Internet infrastructure and to design a variety of applications.\n**Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**\nIn this module, you’ll build on prior knowledge of software engineering principles, expanding it to include a more thorough understanding of what constitutes good design. You’ll learn how design can be improved using patterns and refactoring, and you’ll gain a broad appreciation of the different architectural styles used in modern software.\n**MSc Project – 60 credits**\nYou’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project is one of the most satisfying elements of this course. It allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem, and it can be used to explore and develop your specific interests.\nRecent projects include:\n  * Intelligent services to support sensemaking\n  * Machine Learning based cloud resource scheduling\n  * Energy-aware resource management\n  * Scalable serverless workflows\n\n\nA proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.\n#### Optional modules\nPlease note: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.\n**Data Science – 15 credits**\nThe aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data. You’ll cover the theoretical basis of a variety of approaches, placed into a practical context using different application domains.\n**Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**\nThis module provides a comprehensive knowledge on fundamentals and practical aspects of distributed ledgers and their applications in society. Starting from required knowledge on distributed systems and security, this module moves to the “big picture” of the different blockchain architectures that have been evolving in this dynamic technological landscape.\n**Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**\nYou’ll learn how to analyse descriptions of complex real-world scenarios in terms of formal representation languages, understanding automated reasoning and ontology as well as their applications.\n**Machine Learning – 15 credits**\nOn completion of this module, you should be able to: list the principal algorithms used in machine learning and derive their update rules appreciate the capabilities and limitations of current approaches; evaluate the performance of machine learning algorithms; and use existing implementation(s) of machine learning algorithms to explore data sets and build models.\n**Deep Learning – 15 credits**\nThis module will equip you with a state-of-the-art understanding of Deep Learning, and highly practical skills and expertise in the construction of AI systems, including those that integrate multiple modalities.\n**Algorithms – 15 credits**\nAlgorithms and algorithmic problem solving are at the heart of computer science. This module introduces the design and analysis of efficient algorithms and data structures. You\'ll learn how to quantify the efficiency of an algorithm and what algorithmic solutions are efficient. You’ll also be taught techniques for designing efficient algorithms, including efficient data structures, standard methods such as Divide-and-Conquer and Dynamic Programming as well as more advanced techniques. This is done using illustrative and fundamental problems relevant to AI.\n**Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**\nThis module is designed to give those with little or no programming experience a firm foundation in programming for data analysis and AI systems. The module will also fully stretch those with substantial prior programming experience (e.g. computer scientists) to extend their programming and system-building knowledge through self-learning supported by online courseware.\n**Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**\nThis module will provide you with an introduction to linguistic theory and terminology. On competition you should be able to: demonstrate an understanding and how to use algorithms and resources for implementing and evaluating text mining and analytics systems; develop solutions using open-source and commercial toolkits; and consider the applications of data mining and text analytics through case studies in information retrieval and extraction.\n**Scientific Computation – 15 credits**\nThis module will support your understanding of the range of problems that can be formulated as nonlinear equation systems. On completion, you should be able to: consider standard algorithms for these problems and the efficiency of their implementation; and demonstrate how state-of-the-art algorithms deliver gains in efficiency and allow the solution of large, sparse systems of nonlinear equations.\n#### Enhance Your Academic and Subject-Specific Language\nAs part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0) that provides valuable insights into studying a postgraduate degree in the UK while helping you develop your academic and subject-specific vocabulary.\nThrough a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study, you will explore the use of technology—such as translation tools and generative AI—to support effective communication. You will also build the language and literacy skills necessary to become a more confident and capable communicator throughout your studies.\n[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Cloud Computing) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FC-FT)\n### Learning and teaching\nOur [groundbreaking research](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-research-innovation) feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff who are at the forefront of their disciplines. You’ll have regular contact with them through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings.\nIndependent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.\n#### **Specialist facilities**\nAt Leeds, we provide an exciting environment in which to gain a range of skills and experience cutting-edge technology.\nYou’ll benefit from world-class facilities to support your learning, including:\n  * a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource consisting of several clusters which are used for all forms of predictive modelling, data analysis and simulation\n  * Access to Microsoft Azure cloud\n  * a visualisation lab including a Powerwall, benchtop display with tracking system, WorldViz PPT optical tracking system and Intersense InertiaCube orientation tracker\n  * Ascension Flock of Birds tracking systems, three DOF and 6DOF Phantom force feedback devices\n  * Twin Immersion Corp CyberGloves\n  * rendering cluster and labs containing both Microsoft and Linux platforms, among others.\n  * excellent facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building. [Explore more of our facilities through our 360 virtual experience.](http://explore.leeds.ac.uk)\n\n\n#### **Programme team**\nOn this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus.\n### Assessment\nYou’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods. \n## Applying\n### Entry requirements\nA bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in computer science.\nWe require all applicants to have studied a breadth of relevant modules including significant programming, systems development, data structures and algorithms.\nApplicants with any of the following will be considered on a case-by-case basis:\n  * A bachelor degree with a 2:1 (hons) in other computing-based degrees.\n  * A bachelor degree with a 2:2 (hons) in computer science, with at least three years of relevant experience.\n  * Professional qualifications and relevant experience.\n\n\n#### International\nWe accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications). For more information please contact the Admissions Team.\n#### English language requirements\nIELTS 6.5 overall, with no less than 6.0 in any component. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").\n**Improve your English**\nInternational students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study our postgraduate pre-sessional English course, to help improve your English language level.\nThis pre-sessional course is designed with a progression route to your degree programme and you’ll learn academic English in the context of your subject area. To find out more, read [Language for Engineering (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i193/language-for-engineering) and [Language for Science: Engineering (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i194/language-for-science-engineering). \nWe also offer online pre-sessionals alongside our on-campus pre-sessionals. Find out more about our [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-) and our [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-). \nYou can also study pre-sessionals for longer periods – read about our [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).\n### How to apply\n**Application deadlines**\nPlease read our [How to Apply page](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing-masters/doc/apply-13) for full details, including application deadlines and what to include with your application.\nApplicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.\n**31 July 2026** – International applicants \n**11 September 2026** – UK applicants \nClick below to access the University’s online application system and find out more about the application process.\n### [ Apply](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmyleedsportal.leeds.ac.uk%2Fsignin-landing&data=05%7C02%7CA.C.Rout%40leeds.ac.uk%7C4f8edcbaccdb42bbbecb08dce7a5e273%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638639946885795283%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=45OzXEzfTuOORMbMejP6n9cR8i%2B5MO3VgqQr8weM3H8%3D&reserved=0)\nIf you\'re still unsure about the application process, contact the admissions team for help.\nRead about visas, immigration and other information in [International students](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/international/ "International students"). We recommend that international students apply as early as possible to ensure that they have time to apply for their visa.\n### Admissions policy\n[University of Leeds Admissions Policy 2026](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/study/doc/university-leeds-admissions-policy-2026-27)\n### This course is taught by\n[School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing)\n### Contact us\nPostgraduate Admissions team\nEmail: pgcomp@leeds.ac.uk\n## Fees\nUK: £14,250 (Total)\nInternational: £34,250 (Total)\nRead more about [paying fees and charges](https://students.leeds.ac.uk/pay-fees "paying fees and charges").\nFor fees information for international taught postgraduate students, read [Masters fees](http://www.leeds.ac.uk/pgtfees/).\n### Additional cost information\nThere may be additional costs related to your course or programme of study, or related to being a student at the University of Leeds. Links between the taught modules and our research provide our students with added strengths in artificial intelligence, intelligent systems, distributed systems, and the analysis of complex data. As a result, you’ll be well-prepared for a range of careers, as well as further research at PhD level.\nPlus, the University of Leeds is in the top 5 most targeted universities in the UK by graduate recruiters, according to [High Fliers’ The Graduate Market in 2024 report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/).\nHere’s an insight into some of the job positions and organisations previous advanced computer science graduates have secured:\n  * Technical Graduate, Thomson Reuters\n  * Engineer, Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory\n  * Senior Software Engineer, Funding Circle\n  * Technical Developer, Reading Room\n  * Head of Audience Development, Al Jazeera Media Network\n  * Systems Engineer, Systematic\n  * Software Engineer, THG\n  * Programmer, Alibaba\n\n\n### Careers support\nAt Leeds, we help you to prepare for your future from day one.
